## 3-15-5 GE USB Control Panel Driver Loss

NOTE: While the loss of drivers should not happen with the current application software loading
process, this section remains as a reference.

Sometimes, after loading new software (or the first time load of software), the GE Front Panel may not
function after Applications (echoloader) has brought the system up in scan mode. The alpha-numeric
keyboard, trackball and two set keys will function but the touch panel and all other GE controls on the
operator interface will NOT function.

Watch the system closely as the system boots up. Early in the process, during the BIOS load, the front
panel lights will flash yellow then green and go out. This basically means the front panel is "healthy" or
functional.

During the Applications loading process of boot up, when the blue bar on the image monitor is about 2/
3rds of the way complete, the front panel lights will flash again. This basically confirms USB
communication with the front panel.

During the software load process, the USB driver for the GE Control Panel may get corrupted. A simple
Windows Driver Upgrade (update) will cure the problem.

This is expected behavior of that setting, not a colorization failure.

With:

```json
"editor.bracketPairColorization.independentColorPoolPerBracketType": true
```

each bracket type (`()`, `[]`, `{}`) has its own color sequence. In typical C++ nesting where types alternate, every type is at its first level—so they all receive `bracketPairColor1` (often yellow).

To color by overall nesting depth, use:

```json
"editor.bracketPairColorization.independentColorPoolPerBracketType": false
```

The same conclusion is documented in user reports of this setting’s behavior: [Stack Overflow discussion](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/73758066/editor-bracketpaircolorization-enabled-true-only-colorizing-one-nesting-level).
